reason: The 5% fee instead of 25% is a genuinely good number and I like that more of it goes to the person doing the work, but 'identity verification' isn't the same thing as 'this person is actually good at the job' -- Urban Company at least feels like it's checked that. I'm not letting a stranger into my house or tutoring something important on an app nobody I know has used yet.
objection: Verified ID just means they are who they say they are, not that they won't mess up the plumbing or show up late. I have no reviews, ratings, or completed-job history to go on, and that's the thing I actually check before booking anyone unfamiliar.
would_change_my_mind: If a neighbour or relative had actually used it and it went fine, or if the app showed real ratings/completed-job counts per freelancer so I could judge quality myself, not just that they passed an ID check.
